estimators.ratio: paired per round: the first-named arm's ns per operation over the second's, so a value below 1 means the first-named arm is faster. The point is the geometric mean of the per-round ratios and the interval is BCa 95% on the per-round log ratios (2000 resamples), which is not the quotient of the two per-arm medians. In the concurrent artifact `scaling` is throughput at W readers over throughput at 1 reader, paired per round, mean with BCa 95% on the per-round quotients, and `clone_per_reader_over_sync_locked` is a throughput ratio (above 1 = the cloned readers do more)
estimators.columns: `ns_per_op` and `ops_per_s` are medians over the cell's round processes of that round's one timed pass; the memory census publishes exact requested bytes, one count per cell
estimators.raw: every timed cell carries rounds_raw, one row per (round process, arm) with that process's load window; the memory census (under `memory`) has no rounds

provenance.host_description: 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-12900F (24 threads, 30 MiB L3, Linux 6.8.0-138-generic)
